# Cover Letter Template

A cover letter is not strictly mandatory but **strongly recommended**. It's where you tell the consular officer, in your own words, **why you're going + when you'll return**. A clear cover letter shortens the officer's decision-making and reduces the chance of an "interview required" follow-up.

> **Style guidance:** Plain, direct, factual. **Not a sales pitch.** Don't be flowery or emotional. A French consulate officer reads dozens of these per hour — make yours easy to skim.

---

## Format

- Printed on **plain paper** (A4 or US Letter — both fine).
- **Single page**, single-sided.
- Standard business letter format: your address top-right, recipient address top-left, date, salutation, body, signature.
- Either French or English. **French is preferred** if you can write it correctly; otherwise English is fine for UK/Anglophone applicants.

---

## Template (replace placeholders, print, sign)

```
{{YOUR_FULL_NAME}}
{{YOUR_HOME_STREET}}
{{YOUR_HOME_CITY}}, {{YOUR_POSTCODE}}
{{YOUR_HOME_COUNTRY}}
Phone: {{YOUR_PHONE}}
Email: {{YOUR_EMAIL}}

Consulate General of France
(via TLScontact {{TLS_CENTRE}})

{{LETTER_DATE_E.G. "23 May 2026"}}


Subject: Schengen short-stay visa application — {{YOUR_FULL_NAME}}
         France-Visas reference: {{FRANCE_VISAS_REFERENCE}}
         Travel dates: {{DEPARTURE_DATE}} to {{RETURN_DATE}}


Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for a short-stay Schengen visa to visit France from
{{DEPARTURE_DATE}} to {{RETURN_DATE}}, a total of {{TRIP_DURATION_DAYS}}
days.

The purpose of my trip is {{TRIP_PURPOSE_ONE_SENTENCE}}.

My planned itinerary is:

  - {{DATE_1}}: arrive at {{ARRIVAL_AIRPORT}} from {{ORIGIN_CITY}};
                stay at {{ACCOMMODATION_1}} in {{CITY_1}}.
  - {{DATES_RANGE_2}}: {{ACTIVITY_OR_LOCATION_2}}.
  - {{DATES_RANGE_3}}: {{ACTIVITY_OR_LOCATION_3}}.
  - {{RETURN_DATE}}: depart from {{DEPARTURE_AIRPORT}} back to
                     {{HOME_COUNTRY}}.

I confirm that:

  - I will return to {{HOME_COUNTRY}} on {{RETURN_DATE}} and resume
    my employment at {{EMPLOYER_NAME}} (employment letter enclosed).
  - I have travel insurance covering medical expenses of at least
    €30,000 valid in the entire Schengen area for the full duration
    of my trip (certificate enclosed).
  - My accommodation in France is confirmed and paid (booking
    confirmations enclosed).
  - I have sufficient funds to cover the trip ({{SUFFICIENT_FUNDS_AMOUNT_GBP}}
    available in my account; bank statements enclosed).
  - {{ANY_OTHER_RELEVANT_CONFIRMATION}}

Thank you for considering my application. I am happy to provide any
additional information you may require.

Yours faithfully,



{{YOUR_FULL_NAME}}
(handwritten signature above)
```

---

## Variants by purpose

### If visiting family or friends, replace the "purpose" sentence with:

> The purpose of my trip is to visit {{HOST_NAME}}, my {{RELATIONSHIP}} (e.g. mother / brother / close friend), who lives at {{FRANCE_ADDRESS}}. An *Attestation d'Accueil* validated by the *mairie* is enclosed.

### If business / conference, replace with:

> The purpose of my trip is to attend {{CONFERENCE_OR_MEETING_NAME}} held in {{FRENCH_CITY}} from {{START_DATE}} to {{END_DATE}}. The invitation letter from {{HOST_COMPANY}} is enclosed. My employer ({{EMPLOYER_NAME}}) has approved this trip and continues to employ me upon return; the employment letter is enclosed.

### If you're a freelancer / self-employed, add:

> I am self-employed as a {{PROFESSION}}. My most recent tax return (year ending {{TAX_YEAR}}) is enclosed, along with bank statements showing my business income for the last 6 months.

### If you're a retiree, replace the "employment" line with:

> I am retired. My pension statement from {{PENSION_PROVIDER}} (showing {{MONTHLY_AMOUNT_GBP}} per month) is enclosed. My home address remains {{HOME_ADDRESS}} and I plan to return there on {{RETURN_DATE}}.

### If you've been refused a Schengen visa before, add a brief paragraph:

> I would like to note that my previous Schengen application of {{PREVIOUS_DATE}} was refused. Since then, {{HOW_CIRCUMSTANCES_CHANGED}}. I have enclosed [specific documents] to address the reasons cited in the previous refusal.

---

## Common pitfalls

| Pitfall | Why it hurts |
|---|---|
| Letter too long (more than one page) | Reviewer skim-reads; key facts get lost. Cut everything that isn't directly relevant. |
| Vague return commitment ("I plan to return after the trip") | Make the return concrete: a specific date, with employment / family ties / property ownership backing it up. |
| Promises that contradict the rest of the application | If your cover letter says "two weeks" but France-Visas says "four weeks," that's an automatic flag. **Cross-check dates** with what you submitted in Phase 1. |
| Emotional language ("I'm desperate to see Paris") | Sounds like a flight risk. Stick to facts. |
| Missing signature | Always sign by hand below the typed name. |
| Date in wrong format | Use the date format common in the consulate's country (UK/EU: DD Month YYYY). Avoid all-numeric dates like 05/06/2026 (ambiguous between US/EU formats). |
| Copy-pasted from a generic template visibly | Sample-text giveaways like `[YOUR NAME HERE]` left in. **Search-and-replace every `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` before printing.** |

---

## Quality check before printing

- [ ] Every `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` has been replaced with real data.
- [ ] Dates are consistent with your France-Visas application and TLScontact booking.
- [ ] Return commitment is explicit and credible.
- [ ] Names match passport spelling exactly.
- [ ] Letter is single page.
- [ ] Signature space + room to handwrite name underneath.
- [ ] Printed on clean A4/Letter paper, no smudges, no creases.
- [ ] One physical copy per applicant (each applicant in a family needs their own — adapted as appropriate; e.g. children's letters can reference their parents).
